findings.explanation: IssueBulkUpdateDateEndpoint.post() fetches issues using only user-controlled issue IDs without verifying they belong to the authorized project. Line 1103 queries Issue.objects.filter(id__in=issue_ids) with no project_id or workspace_id filter, allowing a user with PROJECT membership to update issues from any project by providing arbitrary issue IDs. The @allow_permission decorator only validates the user has PROJECT membership in the specified project, but does not constrain the fetched issues to that project.

The allow_permission decorator validates role membership in a specific project (lines 43-50: ProjectMember.objects.filter(member=request.user, workspace__slug=kwargs['slug'], project_id=kwargs['project_id'], ...) but does not enforce that fetched resources belong to that project.

findings.suggested_fix: Filter the Issue query to include the project_id constraint: Issue.objects.filter(id__in=issue_ids, project_id=project_id) to ensure only issues from the authorized project can be updated.

findings.explanation: The 'order_by' request parameter is obtained directly from user input (line 1060: request.GET.get('order_by', '-created_at')) and passed to order_issue_queryset() which may use it directly in Django's .order_by() method (line 82 in order_queryset.py) without proper validation. While only specific field patterns are allowed in the if/elif conditions, any value that doesn't match those conditions reaches line 82 and is passed to .order_by(order_by_param) without validation, allowing an attacker to inject arbitrary ordering expressions that could execute unintended SQL.

findings.suggested_fix: Add an allowlist validation before using order_by_param in the else clause. Implement a strict allowlist of permitted ordering fields and reject any order_by_param values that don't match the allowlist. For example: allowed_order_by = ['created_at', '-created_at', 'updated_at', '-updated_at', ...] and validate order_by_param against this list before line 82.

findings.explanation: The IssueBulkUpdateDateEndpoint fetches issues by user-controlled IDs from the request data (line 1099: `issue_ids = [update["id"] for update in updates]`) and filters them only by workspace slug and project_id (line 1103: `Issue.objects.filter(id__in=issue_ids)`). There is no verification that the issues belong to the requested project or that the requester has access to them. The @allow_permission decorator only checks if the user is an ADMIN or MEMBER role, but does not validate project membership or ownership. A user with MEMBER role in one project could potentially update issues in another project by providing their IDs.

# Security policy
This document outlines the security protocols and vulnerability reporting guidelines for the Plane project. Ensuring the security of our systems is a top priority, and while we work diligently to maintain robust protection, vulnerabilities may still occur. We highly value the community’s role in identifying and reporting security concerns to uphold the integrity of our systems and safeguard our users.

## Reporting a vulnerability
If you have identified a security vulnerability, submit your findings to [security@plane.so](mailto:security@plane.so). 
Ensure your report includes all relevant information needed for us to reproduce and assess the issue. Include the IP address or URL of the affected system.

To ensure a responsible and effective disclosure process, please adhere to the following:

- Maintain confidentiality and refrain from publicly disclosing the vulnerability until we have had the opportunity to investigate and address the issue.
- Refrain from running automated vulnerability scans on our infrastructure or dashboard without prior consent. Contact us to set up a sandbox environment if necessary.
- Do not exploit any discovered vulnerabilities for malicious purposes, such as accessing or altering user data.
- Do not engage in physical security attacks, social engineering, distributed denial of service (DDoS) attacks, spam campaigns, or attacks on third-party applications as part of your vulnerability testing.

## Out of scope
While we appreciate all efforts to assist in improving our security, please note that the following types of vulnerabilities are considered out of scope:

- Vulnerabilities requiring man-in-the-middle (MITM) attacks or physical access to a user’s device.
- Content spoofing or text injection issues without a clear attack vector or the ability to modify HTML/CSS.
- Issues related to email spoofing.
- Missing DNSSEC, CAA, or CSP headers.
- Absence of secure or HTTP-only flags on non-sensitive cookies.

# Security policy
This document outlines the security protocols and vulnerability reporting guidelines for the Plane project. Ensuring the security of our systems is a top priority, and while we work diligently to maintain robust protection, vulnerabilities may still occur. We highly value the community’s role in identifying and reporting security concerns to uphold the integrity of our systems and safeguard our users.

## Reporting a vulnerability
If you have identified a security vulnerability, submit your findings to [security@plane.so](mailto:security@plane.so). 
Ensure your report includes all relevant information needed for us to reproduce and assess the issue. Include the IP address or URL of the affected system.

To ensure a responsible and effective disclosure process, please adhere to the following:

- Maintain confidentiality and refrain from publicly disclosing the vulnerability until we have had the opportunity to investigate and address the issue.
- Refrain from running automated vulnerability scans on our infrastructure or dashboard without prior consent. Contact us to set up a sandbox environment if necessary.
- Do not exploit any discovered vulnerabilities for malicious purposes, such as accessing or altering user data.
- Do not engage in physical security attacks, social engineering, distributed denial of service (DDoS) attacks, spam campaigns, or attacks on third-party applications as part of your vulnerability testing.

## Out of scope
While we appreciate all efforts to assist in improving our security, please note that the following types of vulnerabilities are considered out of scope:

- Vulnerabilities requiring man-in-the-middle (MITM) attacks or physical access to a user’s device.
- Content spoofing or text injection issues without a clear attack vector or the ability to modify HTML/CSS.
- Issues related to email spoofing.
- Missing DNSSEC, CAA, or CSP headers.
- Absence of secure or HTTP-only flags on non-sensitive cookies.

# Security policy
This document outlines the security protocols and vulnerability reporting guidelines for the Plane project. Ensuring the security of our systems is a top priority, and while we work diligently to maintain robust protection, vulnerabilities may still occur. We highly value the community’s role in identifying and reporting security concerns to uphold the integrity of our systems and safeguard our users.

## Reporting a vulnerability
If you have identified a security vulnerability, submit your findings to [security@plane.so](mailto:security@plane.so). 
Ensure your report includes all relevant information needed for us to reproduce and assess the issue. Include the IP address or URL of the affected system.

To ensure a responsible and effective disclosure process, please adhere to the following:

- Maintain confidentiality and refrain from publicly disclosing the vulnerability until we have had the opportunity to investigate and address the issue.
- Refrain from running automated vulnerability scans on our infrastructure or dashboard without prior consent. Contact us to set up a sandbox environment if necessary.
- Do not exploit any discovered vulnerabilities for malicious purposes, such as accessing or altering user data.
- Do not engage in physical security attacks, social engineering, distributed denial of service (DDoS) attacks, spam campaigns, or attacks on third-party applications as part of your vulnerability testing.

## Out of scope
While we appreciate all efforts to assist in improving our security, please note that the following types of vulnerabilities are considered out of scope:

- Vulnerabilities requiring man-in-the-middle (MITM) attacks or physical access to a user’s device.
- Content spoofing or text injection issues without a clear attack vector or the ability to modify HTML/CSS.
- Issues related to email spoofing.
- Missing DNSSEC, CAA, or CSP headers.
- Absence of secure or HTTP-only flags on non-sensitive cookies.
